course.title: Calculus and Optimisation for Machine Learning
course.tagline: Differentiate by hand and in code, build a small reverse-mode engine, and train models with gradient descent you can diagnose
course.description: Participants work through the calculus that trains models: derivatives as local linear approximations, gradients, Jacobians and the chain rule on computational graphs. They backpropagate by hand, then write a small reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine and check it against a framework. They run batch, stochastic and momentum gradient descent, read loss curves, and handle convexity and constraints. The capstone trains a small network with their own engine; tensor-level differentiation and modern optimisers follow in SPC-DLR-302.
course.audience: Beginners. Career changers and non-computing graduates closing bridging gaps before advanced study, and computing graduates refreshing the mathematics behind models; a placement test lets participants skip any course whose content they already command.
prerequisites: FND-MTH-101 Linear Algebra for Machine Learning
School calculus: derivatives of polynomials and exponentials, or the pre-work refresher
Writes short Python programs with functions and loops (FND-PRG-101 or equivalent)
course.format_note: Extended: 8 weeks part-time, one session and one lab a week, weekly graded problem sets and a capstone

outcomes.text: Explain derivatives, partial derivatives, gradients and Jacobians as local linear approximations, given functions of one and several variables
outcomes.evidence: supervised AI-off test, at least 70% correct

outcomes.text: Distinguish convex from non-convex objectives and describe how saddle points and step size shape gradient descent, given six loss surfaces with optimisation traces
outcomes.evidence: annotated plots marked against a reference

outcomes.text: Explain how a constraint moves the optimum of a small problem, using the Lagrangian and the meaning of its multiplier, given three problems, including a budget allocation
outcomes.evidence: written solutions marked against a rubric, with each multiplier read as the price of the constraint

outcomes.text: Compute gradients of a composite function by applying the chain rule backwards through a computational graph, given a two-example logistic-regression loss
outcomes.evidence: a hand-worked backward pass matching a numerical gradient check

outcomes.text: Implement reverse-mode automatic differentiation for scalar operations and verify it with finite-difference checks, given a starter interface and test suite
outcomes.evidence: an engine that passes the tests and agrees with a framework's gradients

outcomes.text: Apply batch, stochastic and momentum gradient descent and diagnose divergence or slow convergence from loss curves, given losses on public data
outcomes.evidence: an experiment log with learning-rate sweeps and a diagnosis of each failed run

case_study.name: The adult learning charity
case_study.summary: A non-profit that runs evening literacy and numeracy classes for adults in five districts, D1 to D5, of one city; its own labs use synthetic data generated with a fixed seed: 600 learners coded LR-0001 to LR-0600, five district outreach response curves and a budget, with planted problems (a wrong hand-coded derivative, logits that overflow, separable placement data and districts that a proxy objective starves). The gradient-descent lab and the capstone train on public datasets from the UCI Machine Learning Repository (CC BY 4.0), downloaded when the lab runs and never presented as the charity's data; people appear only as roles.

days.label: Week 1
days.title: Change and approximation
days.subtitle: Derivatives as local linear approximations, and three ways to compute one

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Derivatives as local lines
sessions.summary: A derivative is the slope of the best straight-line fit near a point; you compute it by hand, symbolically and numerically
outcomes: Explain a derivative as the slope of the best local linear approximation
Compute derivatives by rule, with symbolic algebra and with finite differences
Choose a finite-difference step by weighing truncation against rounding error

lab.title: Three ways to a derivative
lab.summary: Analytic, symbolic and finite-difference derivatives compared across step sizes

steps.text: Derive three derivatives by hand and code them
Get the same derivatives from SymPy and compare
Write forward and central differences
Sweep the step from 0.1 to 1e-12 and plot the error
Explain the V: truncation against rounding, and the best step
Test how far the tangent line and the quadratic hold
Write three findings in the lab log

lab.stretch: Compute the complex-step derivative and see why it has no rounding V

days.label: Week 2
days.title: Several variables
days.subtitle: Partial derivatives, gradients and Jacobians, and how to check them

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Gradients and Jacobians
sessions.summary: Hold all inputs but one still to get a partial derivative; stack them into a gradient, or into a Jacobian for a map with several outputs
outcomes: Compute partial derivatives and assemble the gradient of a function of several variables
Explain the gradient as the direction of steepest increase and a Jacobian as the best local linear map
Check a hand-derived gradient or Jacobian with central differences and a relative-error tolerance

lab.title: Gradients and a Jacobian, checked
lab.summary: Partial derivatives, a gradient, two Jacobians and a reusable gradient checker on the charity's completion and enrolment models

steps.text: Derive the partial derivatives of the completion model
Build the gradient and test the steepest direction
Write a gradient checker for any function of n inputs
Build two Jacobians and check them
Predict a budget shift with the Jacobian and compare
Find the planted wrong partial derivative
Write three findings in the lab log

lab.stretch: Check the symmetry of second partial derivatives numerically

days.label: Week 3
days.title: The chain rule on graphs
days.subtitle: Computational graphs, forward and reverse mode, and a backward pass by hand

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Graphs and the chain rule
sessions.summary: Write a loss as a graph of simple operations; the chain rule run backwards gives every gradient in one pass
outcomes: Draw the computational graph of a composite function
Explain why reverse mode costs one backward pass per output and forward mode one pass per input
Compute a backward pass by hand and confirm it with a numerical gradient check

lab.title: Backpropagation by hand
lab.summary: Backpropagation by hand on a tiny logistic regression, checked in code

steps.text: Draw the graph of the two-example loss
Fill in the forward pass by hand
Run the backward pass by hand
Check your forward pass in code
Match a numerical gradient check
One directional derivative in forward mode
Write where your values differed, and why

lab.stretch: Add an L2 term and extend the backward pass by hand

days.label: Week 4
days.title: Reverse mode in code
days.subtitle: The chain rule with vectors and matrices, and a small automatic differentiation engine

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: A reverse-mode engine
sessions.summary: Reverse mode multiplies vector-Jacobian products from the output back; a small engine records operations and replays them backwards
outcomes: Apply the chain rule to vector functions as products of Jacobians
Design a scalar reverse-mode engine: nodes, local derivatives, topological order and accumulation
Verify an engine with finite-difference checks and against a framework's gradients

lab.title: A scalar reverse-mode engine
lab.summary: A scalar reverse-mode differentiation engine built and tested

steps.text: Read the interface and run the test suite
Implement addition, multiplication and backward
Add power, exp, log, tanh and ReLU
Pass the finite-difference checks on random expressions
Compare your gradients with a framework's
Fix gradient accumulation for a reused node
Write three findings in the lab log

lab.stretch: Add a dot-product node with its vector-Jacobian product

days.label: Week 5
days.title: Gradient descent
days.subtitle: Step size, stochastic gradients, momentum and reading loss curves

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Descent and loss curves
sessions.summary: Gradient descent steps against the gradient; the step size, the batch and momentum decide whether a run converges, crawls or diverges
outcomes: Apply batch, mini-batch stochastic and momentum gradient descent
Describe what adaptive step methods, warm-up and decay change
Diagnose divergence, oscillation and slow convergence from a loss curve

lab.title: Learning-rate sweeps
lab.summary: Learning-rate sweeps for three gradient descent variants on public regression data

steps.text: Load the public data, split it and find the reference loss
Sweep the learning rate for batch gradient descent
Sweep it for mini-batch stochastic gradient descent
Sweep it for momentum
Run on unscaled features and diagnose
Write the experiment log with a diagnosis per run
Add warm-up and step decay to the noisy run

lab.stretch: Add an adaptive step method and compare its sweep

days.label: Week 6
days.title: The shape of a loss
days.subtitle: Convexity, saddle points, curvature and the largest stable step

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Convexity and curvature
sessions.summary: The Hessian tells a minimum from a saddle and bounds the step size; convex losses have no traps, non-convex ones do
outcomes: Distinguish convex from non-convex objectives with a test you can run
Classify critical points from the eigenvalues of the Hessian
Relate the largest stable step to the largest curvature

lab.title: Six loss surfaces
lab.summary: Six loss surfaces with gradient-descent traces, classified and annotated

steps.text: Plot the six surfaces as contour maps
Classify critical points from the Hessian
Test each surface for convexity
Trace gradient descent below, at and above the stable step
Start on and off the saddle's ridge
Annotate each plot against the reference
Write three findings in the lab log

lab.stretch: Take Newton steps on the valley and compare with gradient descent

days.label: Week 7
days.title: Stable losses and penalties
days.subtitle: Log-sum-exp, softmax cross-entropy and regularisation as a penalty

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Stable losses and penalties
sessions.summary: Shift logits before exponentiating, use the clean gradient of softmax cross-entropy, and add a penalty to change the shape of the loss
outcomes: Compute softmax and log-sum-exp without overflow
Derive and check the gradient of softmax cross-entropy
Explain regularisation as a penalty that reshapes the loss and bounds the weights

lab.title: Stable softmax and a penalty
lab.summary: A stable three-level placement model, trained with and without an L2 penalty

steps.text: Watch naive softmax overflow on the planted logits
Write stable log-sum-exp, softmax and cross-entropy
Check the gradient of softmax cross-entropy
Train the placement model with gradient descent
Add an L2 penalty and sweep its strength
Compare weight norms and held-out loss
Write three findings in the lab log

lab.stretch: Show that the penalised loss is strictly convex while the plain one is not

days.label: Week 8
days.title: Constraints
days.subtitle: Lagrange multipliers, projected gradients and the price of a constraint

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Constraints and prices
sessions.summary: A constraint moves the optimum; the Lagrange multiplier prices it, and projected gradients reach the same answer by stepping and projecting
outcomes: Solve a small equality-constrained problem with the Lagrangian
Read a multiplier as the price of its constraint
Explain how optimising a convenient proxy can harm the people a model serves

lab.title: A budget allocation two ways
lab.summary: A budget allocation solved with Lagrange multipliers and with projected gradients

steps.text: Write the Lagrangian for two districts and solve it by hand
Solve the five-district problem from the Lagrange conditions
Solve it again with projected gradient ascent
Compare the answers and read the multiplier
Find who the proxy leaves out and add a floor
Write the recommendation for the finance officer

lab.stretch: Weight each district by need and see how the multiplier moves

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone oral checks
days.subtitle: A two-layer network trained with your own engine, defended in ten minutes with the questions inside them

capstone.summary: A two-layer network trained on public data with the participant's own engine, with gradient checks, three optimisers compared across seeds and every run reported, defended in a ten-minute oral check
capstone.submission: A link to a public GitHub repository with the participant's engine, its tests and gradient checks, the training code, the log of every run with its seed and the report; then a ten-minute oral check, questions included, in which the participant traces a backward pass through their engine and explains a failed run from the log

rubric.criterion: Engine correct: passes the course test suite and the gradient checks on the network
Network trained on the public data with a held-out split, reproducible from the seeds
Three optimisers compared across at least three seeds, with loss curves and held-out accuracy
Every run, seed and failure reported, not the best result alone
A written diagnosis of each failed run from its loss curve and log
